description: Original compact Phase 2 practice bank; not copied textbook exercises. Deterministic marking; authored content is not independently peer-reviewed.

questions.title: Moment conversion
questions.prompt: Convert 3 kN·m to N·mm. Enter a value and choose its unit.
hints: Convert the force and the length separately.

questions.title: Equivalent stress units
questions.prompt: A positive bending moment is 18 kN·m and the elastic section modulus is 666,666.7 mm³. Calculate the signed elastic stress M / W_el. Enter the value in any listed unit.
hints: Convert the moment into N·mm before dividing by W_el in mm³.
questions.solution:
M = 18 kN·m = 18,000,000 N·mm.
Stress = 18,000,000 N·mm / 666,666.7 mm³ = approximately 27 MPa = 0.027 GPa.

questions.title: Pin and roller reactions
questions.prompt: A horizontal beam has an ideal pin at A and a frictionless roller on a horizontal surface at B. Which support reactions belong on its free-body diagram?

options.a: A horizontal and vertical; B vertical.
options.b: A and B each resist a moment.
options.c: A vertical only; B horizontal only.

hints: Identify the translation each support restrains.
The ideal pin provides two force components; this roller provides one vertical component.
questions.solution: Show A horizontal and vertical reactions and B vertical reaction. Ideal pin and roller do not apply reaction couples.
questions.reference: Background reference: R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th edition (2015), section 2.4, printed page 50; 001-180.pdf page 71. The question is original, not a textbook exercise.

questions.title: Isolating a beam
questions.prompt: You remove a supported beam from its surroundings to draw its free-body diagram. What replaces the supports?

options.a: The applied support forces and any support moments permitted by the idealisation.
options.b: Nothing; supports have no forces once removed.
options.c: Only the applied loads, not the support actions.

hints: The isolated body must still represent the actions of its surroundings.
Replace each removed restraint by its permitted reaction components.
questions.solution: Isolate the beam, show applied loads and replace supports with the forces and moments consistent with the support idealisations.
questions.reference: Background reference: R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th edition (2015), section 2.4, printed page 50; 001-180.pdf page 71. The question is original, not a textbook exercise.

questions.title: Change the restraint
questions.prompt: If an ideal roller rests against a smooth vertical wall instead of a horizontal surface, what is its single reaction direction?
hints: A smooth contact cannot transmit a friction force.
Its contact force is normal to the surface.
questions.solution: A smooth vertical wall exerts a horizontal normal reaction; it has no tangential friction reaction in this idealisation.
questions.reference: Background reference: R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th edition (2015), section 2.4, printed page 50; 001-180.pdf page 71. The question is original, not a textbook exercise.

questions.title: Find the right reaction
questions.prompt: A horizontal simply supported 6 m beam has an ideal pin at A and a roller at B. A 24 kN downward point load acts 2 m from A. Neglect self-weight. Find the upward vertical reaction at B.
hints: Take moments about A to eliminate the reaction at A.
B is 6 m from A; the load is 2 m from A.
questions.solution:
ΣM about A = 0: R_B × 6 m = 24 kN × 2 m.
R_B = 48 kN·m / 6 m = 8 kN upward.
Check: R_A = 24 kN − 8 kN = 16 kN upward.
questions.reference: Background reference: R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th edition (2015), section 2.4, printed page 50; 001-180.pdf page 71. The question is original, not a textbook exercise.

questions.title: Move the load
questions.prompt: Use the same 6 m simply supported beam and 24 kN downward point load, now 4 m from A. Neglect self-weight. Find the upward reaction at B.
hints: The load moved towards B, so which support should carry more?
Take moments about A: R_B × 6 m = 24 kN × 4 m.
questions.solution:
R_B = 24 kN × 4 m / 6 m = 16 kN upward.
Check: R_A = 24 kN − 16 kN = 8 kN upward.
questions.reference: Background reference: R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th edition (2015), section 2.4, printed page 50; 001-180.pdf page 71. The question is original, not a textbook exercise.

questions.title: Choose a moment centre
questions.prompt: For the beam above, why can taking moments about A eliminate the vertical reaction at A from the moment equation?

options.a: Its line of action passes through A, giving zero perpendicular moment arm.
options.b: The reaction at A is necessarily zero.

hints: A force produces moment through its perpendicular distance from the moment centre.
What is that distance for a force acting at A?
questions.solution: The vertical reaction at A acts through A, so its moment arm about A is zero. It can still be non-zero.
questions.reference: Background reference: R. C. Hibbeler, Structural Analysis, 9th edition (2015), section 2.4, printed page 50; 001-180.pdf page 71. The question is original, not a textbook exercise.
